findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key credentials are embedded in Terraform user data, exposing them in source control, Terraform state/plan artifacts, and EC2 instance user-data retrieval. Anyone obtaining these credentials can use the permissions assigned to that IAM principal.

No metadata_options configuration requires IMDSv2; the instance can use IMDSv1 by default. An SSRF flaw on this internet-facing host could therefore be used to retrieve instance metadata and any attached role credentials.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so its encryption depends on an external account-level default rather than being enforced by this configuration. Data written to the volume may be stored unencrypted at rest.

This snapshot is created from a volume whose encryption is not enforced. EBS snapshots inherit source-volume encryption status, so this configuration can create an unencrypted copy of the volume's data.
TCP port 22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on a publicly addressed instance to the entire internet and enabling broad scanning and brute-force attempts.
All protocols and ports may egress to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised web host can freely communicate with command-and-control infrastructure or exfiltrate data.
The bucket that stores VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Flow-log objects are not guaranteed to be encrypted at rest by this Terraform configuration.
